a.text: It was autumn at the time, and I was trekking through the barren wastes with a few Iberians who were fleeing their homeland.
Just when we thought we were going to meet our ends there, the abbey appeared in front of us. It seemed like some sort of miracle, an act of divine intervention that couldn't be real.
The venerable abbot, Bishop Torregrossa, took in those people who had nowhere to go. He was a respectable elder, most pious and devout in his ways.
Under his management, this monastery, cut off from the rest of the land by the wilderness, became its own fantastical domain of sorts.

Here, people whose lives would normally never intertwine lived in harmony, depending on one another. They lived in material poverty but not spiritual poverty, making no distinction between class, all putting their best feet forward to live life.

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: I knew it, this handwriting...

a.text: When I made my request, the Abbot replied to me after an extended silence, saying that while he would not refuse aid to those in need, there was not much he could do, because of my distance.

Maybe because I wasn't expecting much in the first place, I didn't feel too bad about being turned down. If anything, he seemed be more guilty and chagrined about turning down my unreasonable request than the person who made it in the first place.
I am deeply gratified that there exists such a paradise for good people, but at the same time, I could not help but raise this one question:
Can this miracle, like a seed that refuses to adapt to the soil it is grown in, truly persist on this land?
Maybe I've been here a bit too long.
It's about time I set out again, to Laterano.

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: 'People whose lives would normally never intertwine', 'making no distinction between class'...

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: Yes, when I first saw the scene, I also doubted my eyes, a bit.

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: If I was speaking just for myself, I'd really hope this peace, rare as it is, could last forever.

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: Come in.

steps.name: Monastery Inhabitant
steps.text: Are you busy, Seniora Lemuen?

steps.name: Monastery Inhabitant
steps.text: Remember that pattern you were talking about earlier? Some of the others tried embroidering it onto a quilt with me. How do you think it turned out?

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: Let's see... Mm, hmm. Excellent craftsmanship. It wouldn't surprise me to find it on display in a store.

steps.name: Monastery Inhabitant
steps.text: You're exaggerating.

steps.name: Monastery Inhabitant
steps.text: Now that it's getting colder, the blankets you have with you might not be enough to keep you warm, so everyone pitched in some fabric.

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: I appreciate the concern.

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: But if you give it to me, the others might not have enough? You should think about them first.

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: I know how I look, but I'm actually plenty tough. I don't get sick easily.

steps.name: Monastery Inhabitant
steps.text: Haha, don't worry about us. As long as everyone chips in, it's not a big deal.

steps.name: Monastery Inhabitant
steps.text: But, I must say, I'm not sure 'tough' is what comes to mind when I look at you. What's Laterano thinking these days, sending you so far away?

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: Well, um, about that...

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: It's a question I'd like to ask my superiors.

steps.name: Fortuna
steps.text: Why don't we go back?

steps.name: Delfina
steps.text: Because Raimund and the others can't go with us! Isn't that reason enough?

steps.name: Delfina
steps.text: You want to leave them behind? Well, I don't!

steps.name: Fortuna
steps.text: (Stupid Fina, do you really think I'm that cold-blooded? Of course I'm not going to leave behind the people I grew up with.)

steps.name: Fortuna
steps.text: (But, we can just stay stuck like this forever either. Tempers have really been high lately...)

steps.name: Fortuna
steps.text: (Is there no better solution?)

steps.name: Fortuna
steps.text: *sigh*...
What's wrong? What are you sighing for this time?

steps.name: Raimund
steps.text: That's odd... Why are you here by yourself? Delfina's not with you?

steps.name: Fortuna
steps.text: Raimund!

steps.name: Fortuna
steps.text: What's that supposed to mean? It's not like Delfina and I are stuck together!

steps.name: Raimund
steps.text: You might as well be. You're close enough, just one step from sharing a bed.

steps.name: Fortuna
steps.text: We do sleep together sometimes though... Hey wait, that's not the point!

steps.name: Fortuna
steps.text: When'd you get back anyway? I heard you went hunting with Senior Gerald. Any luck? Didn't get hurt, did you?

steps.name: Fortuna
steps.text: Make sure you let us know if you ever do get hurt. Don't be like Senior Gerald, who just toughs it out by himself.

steps.name: Raimund
steps.text: I'm fine. I don't need you worrying over me for no reason.

steps.name: Fortuna
steps.text: For no reason? Who's the one who said nothing until his wounds got inflamed? And who's the one who went down into the mines without permission and barely made it back?

steps.name: Fortuna
steps.text: You–

steps.name: Raimund
steps.text: I know, I know, let's just say it was my fault, okay?

steps.name: Fortuna
steps.text: Huh? 'Let's just say'?

steps.name: Raimund
steps.text: ...It was my fault.

steps.name: Raimund
steps.text: Fortuna.

steps.name: Fortuna
steps.text: Yes?

steps.name: Raimund
steps.text: Actually, I came back because I wanted to ask you... and Delfina. And of course, the others as well.

steps.name: Raimund
steps.text: I wanted to ask... if you wanted to come with us...?
The young man stopped speaking halfway through.
He suddenly falls silent.

steps.name: Fortuna
steps.text: Raimund?

steps.name: Raimund
steps.text: Never mind, it's no big deal.

steps.name: Raimund
steps.text: I need to leave for a bit, and might not be back until late.

steps.name: Raimund
steps.text: Fortuna, can you come to the roof of the sacrarium before dinner?

steps.name: Raimund
steps.text: Bring Delfina with you too... There's something I need to tell you two.

steps.name: Serpilia
steps.text: Let me take a look. What's going on here?

steps.name: Serpilia
steps.text: They even built a road by the monastery? It stretches all the way to the edge of the city... Is it really so cramped inside? I personally think it's plenty spacious.

steps.name: Richele
steps.text: Are there so many people here? It must be tough feeding a crowd that big... especially out in the barrens.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: See for yourself.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Someone's coming.

steps.name: Serpilia
steps.text: Hmm? Oh, someone just walked out. Should be one of the residents?

steps.name: Raimund
steps.text: Where'd Hyman run off to...?

steps.name: Serpilia
steps.text: Oh? Salvus sis, hottie with a hidden face.

steps.name: Raimund
steps.text: ––! Who's there?!

steps.name: Raimund
steps.text: Halos... You're Sankta.

steps.name: Raimund
steps.text: I don't care who you people are, or what you're after, but you're not coming any closer!

steps.name: Richele
steps.text: Let's not jump right to drawing swords and crossbows. We only just met. Why don't we all take a deep breath and talk things through?

steps.name: Richele
steps.text: Good afternoon, Senior. The three of us here are from Laterano, without any ill intent. No need to be so tense... I'd be pleased as punch if you'd lower your weapon.

steps.name: Raimund
steps.text: What brings some Laterans all the way out to these remote mountains?

steps.name: Richele
steps.text: Um, we were sent by His Holiness in search of two compatriots.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: You're wasting your time, Richele.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: It is clear to me that he knows exactly who we are and why we have come. He has hostile intent.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: You clearly have strong animosity towards Laterano, judging from the displeasure on your face. From where does your hostility come?

steps.name: Raimund
steps.text: ...I have no idea what you're talking about.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: You've been standing by the entrance to the side alley this whole time.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: You're deliberately trying to block our view. You don't want our attention there.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: So, what is in there?

steps.name: Raimund
steps.text: Who do you think you are–

steps.name: Richele
steps.text: Alright, Federico, there's no need to provoke the other side! Though, I'm sure that wasn't your intention.

steps.name: Richele
steps.text: You haven't forgotten the mission His Holiness gave us, right? Low key, low key. We can't afford to make a mess of things again.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: I wasn't trying to provoke anyone.

steps.name: Raimund
steps.text: Hah, you Laterans are always like this. Showing up out of nowhere, making a mess out of everything.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Given the information we have, your situation wasn't looking good to begin with.

steps.name: Raimund
steps.text: ...I dare you to say that again.

steps.name: Raimund
steps.text: Wanna fight? C'mon, I'll show you.

steps.name: Serpilia
steps.text: The air is awfully tense over there...

steps.name: Serpilia
steps.text: Federico has a way of drawing attention. And that makes light work of burglary.

steps.name: Serpilia
steps.text: But, that hooded guy over there... Ugh, something's not right here.

steps.name: Serpilia
steps.text: Forget it, I'll figure out the math later.

steps.name: Serpilia
steps.text: First, I need to find our target.

steps.name: Serpilia
steps.text: Haha, let me guess where you might be, Lemuen.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Looks like no shortage of guests today.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Hello, Senior Gerald.

steps.name: Gerald
steps.text: I thought I'd get to see Stefano here.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: His Excellency still has a lot of business to attend to. He just left.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: He can't have gotten very far, so given your athleticism, I'm sure you could catch up to him.

steps.name: Gerald
steps.text: Thanks.

steps.name: Gerald
steps.text: I haven't heard you hitting the strings today.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: If you enjoy the sound of my music, I don't mind playing something for you right now.

steps.name: Gerald
steps.text: I'll pass.

steps.name: Gerald
steps.text: I'm very grateful... for the joy you've been able to bring some of our people.

steps.name: Gerald
steps.text: But not everyone finds comfort in your music. At least, I don't.

steps.name: Gerald
steps.text: I can't imagine why a musician like you chooses to remain here... But I do hope you won't bring disaster upon us.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: You think too highly of me.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: As far as I know, disasters have always been buried in the soil, from whence they take root, sprout, blossom, and bear fruit.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: If such a seed exists in this garden, it will break through the soil sooner or later.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: And I... am simply a passerby, watching it all unfold.

steps.name: Gerald
steps.text: We have no seeds that ought not sprout.

steps.name: Gerald
steps.text: Before long, everything will return to normal. There will be no accidents, let alone disasters.

steps.name: Gerald
steps.text: All I ask, young lady, is that you don't do anything unnecessary.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Are you giving advice?

steps.name: Gerald
steps.text: No.

steps.name: Gerald
steps.text: I'm giving you a warning.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Such roundabout, insensitive words. Though, I suppose the fact that you haven't done anything means you're holding back, right?

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: I suppose that's to be expected, given the circumstances.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: ...Hmm?

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Oh my.

steps.name: Raggedly-Dressed Boy
steps.text: Pretty...

steps.name: Raggedly-Dressed Girl
steps.text: Ma'am...

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Indeed, no shortage of guests today.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Please come in, my unexpected little visitors.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: My name is Arturia. Would you mind telling me yours?

steps.name: Richele
steps.text: Okay, okay. Stop talking like that, Federico.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: I didn't say anything wrong.

steps.name: Richele
steps.text: Just stay quiet for now, alright?

steps.name: Richele
steps.text: And you, young man, let's not do anything rash. We really are just looking for one of our missing colleagues, and uh, whoever you might be, we mean you no harm.

steps.name: Raimund
steps.text: Hmph. You sure can talk.

steps.name: Raimund
steps.text: That bruiser of yours means me no harm?

steps.name: Richele
steps.text: Ahem, well, you have my word. Either way... could you please let us through? If you could tell the man in charge we're here, that would be ideal.

steps.name: Richele
steps.text: Serpilia... Huh? Where did Serpilia go?

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: She's already inside.

steps.name: Raimund
steps.text: Huh? When she–?!

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Just now.

steps.name: Raimund
steps.text: Gah! I can't let you Laterans run roughshod!

steps.name: Raimund
steps.text: Aren't you here to see the abbot? Come with me!

steps.name: Richele
steps.text: Haha... Great, does that mean you're letting us in?

steps.name: Raimund
steps.text: A warning, first: no running off like that woman–

steps.name: Clément
steps.text: Oh no! Hurry, s-someone!

steps.name: Raimund
steps.text: Clément? What's wrong? What happened?!

steps.name: Clément
steps.text: Thank goodness, Raimund! Let the others know–

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: A raid?

steps.name: Clément
steps.text: Yeah, that's right! Err, Raimund, who are these two?

steps.name: Raimund
steps.text: Don't worry about them! What's going on?!

steps.name: Clément
steps.text: Oh, r-right... It's terrible!

steps.name: Clément
steps.text: I was repairing the windows just now, when I saw something moving in the distance–

steps.name: Clément
steps.text: The band of robbers from before! They're back!
